edits.hebrew: אין בית דין חייבין - דלא הוי הוראה מעליא עד שיורו להתיר בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין שיהא אסור, שהורו להיתר בדבר איסור שאין כתוב בתורה בהדיא:
edits.english: A court is not liable - because it is not a proper ruling until they rule to permit something that the Sadducees do not agree is forbidden, meaning they ruled to permit something forbidden that is not explicitly written in the Torah.

edits.hebrew: זיל קרי בי רב הוא - דכיון דאפשר לו ללמוד ולידע, לא הוי שוגג מעליא וקרוב למזיד הוי:
edits.english: Go learn in a children’s school - because since it is possible for him to learn and know, it is not a proper error, but rather close to an intentional transgression.

Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says: A court is not liable to bring an offering unless it issues an erroneous ruling concerning a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree. For the Sadducees do not accept the Oral Torah, but rather understand the verse as it is written. That is to say, they err in a matter that is not explicitly stated in the Torah, or does not simply derive from the verses. But with regard to a matter with which even the Sadducees agree, they are exempt. What is the reasoning for this exemption? It is a topic that you could go learn in a children’s school. That is to say, this matter is so simple that even children in a children's school know it, and if a court erred in this, it is not considered an error of the court.
And this is not an erroneous ruling, but rather a simple mistake. Or it is a matter of intentional transgression (and see Rashi and Meiri and others).

edits.hebrew: בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו - והא דאצטריך למעוטי כוליה דבר ולא נפיק משום דצדוקין מודין בו. כמו בתו מאנוסתו דלית להו גזירה שווה, או אם חמיו ואם חמותו. ומתניתין דנקט נדה ושבת ועבודת כוכבים לא משום דאהנהו דוקא קאי, אלא רק לפרש קיום מקצת נקטינהו:
edits.english: Concerning a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree - And this is what was necessary to exclude the entire matter, and it does not emerge because the Sadducees agree to it. Like his daughter from a raped woman, for whom they do not have a verbal analogy, or his father-in-law and mother-in-law. And the mishna that mentions Niddah, Shabbat, and idolatry is not because it refers specifically to them, but only to explain the fulfillment of a partial mitzva.
One for one - This means a day for a day.

We learned in the mishna: When are they liable? When they erred and said: There is a prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a menstruating woman written in the Torah, but one who engages in intercourse with a woman who observes a clean day for a day she experiences a discharge is exempt. And it is difficult according to Shmuel's words: And why are they liable for this? The halakha of a woman who observes a day for a day is written in the Torah regarding a niddah not in her menstrual period: “And she shall count for herself” (Leviticus 15:28); this teaches that she counts one clean day for one day (observes a day for a day). If so, the matter is stated in the written Torah, and even the Sadducees agree to it!

edits.hebrew: יש נדה אבל הבא על שומרת יום וכו' - בנדה גופה הוי מצי לאשכוחי הרבה כגון בדם אדום בדם שחור והרבה דחשיב בתורת כהנים. אלא דאתא לאשמועינן אפילו בשומרת יום ובנדה מקרי קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת. ובגמרא דפריך אי הכי אפילו נדה נמי, הכי פירושו: אפילו נדה כגון זה אי הוה בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו הוי קיום מקצת:
edits.english: There is a niddah, but one who engages in intercourse with a woman who observes a day for a day, etc. - Regarding niddah herself, one could find many cases, such as red blood, black blood, and many more listed in Torat Kohanim. Rather, it came to teach us that even regarding a woman who observes a day for a day, and regarding a niddah, it is considered a partial fulfillment and a partial nullification. And regarding the Gemara that asks, 'If so, even a niddah as well,' this is its explanation: Even a niddah in such a case, if it were a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree, it would be a partial fulfillment.

edits.hebrew: הכתיב וספרה לה לא גרסינן, דהא בשמעתא בתרייתא דנדה מפיק לה ממשכב נדתה יהיה לה:
edits.english: The phrase 'it is written: “And she shall count for herself”' we do not learn, for in the last discussion of Niddah, it is derived from 'as the impurity of her niddah shall be for her'.

And they answer: They did not err in the actual law of a woman who observes a day for a day, but rather they said: Ha'ara'ah (the initial stage of intercourse) is permitted with a menstruating woman; it is the completion of intercourse that is forbidden. And they ask: This is also written: “He has uncovered her fount” (Leviticus 20:18), which explicitly states the prohibition of ha'ara'ah with a menstruating woman!
Where they said: In the typical manner it is forbidden - This refers to the completion of intercourse, and in an atypical manner it is permitted.

edits.hebrew: והא - שלא כדרכה נמי כתיב משכבי אשה: שני משכבות, אחד כדרכה ואחד שלא כדרכה:
edits.english: But behold - atypical intercourse is also written: 'the manners in which one lies with a woman': two manners of lying with a woman, one in the typical manner and one in an atypical manner.

And they answer: They said: If one engages in intercourse with her in the typical manner - it is forbidden; if in an atypical manner (anal intercourse) - it is permitted. And they ask: But it is written: “The manners in which one lies with a woman” (Leviticus 18:22), and from here it simply emerges that there are two manners of lying with a woman, in the typical manner and in an atypical manner, and this is as if it is explicitly written!

edits.hebrew: שלא כדרכה נמי הכתיב וכו' - משמע דצדוקין מודין בו. ובפרק אחד דיני ממונות גבי טעה בנואף ונואפת משמע דאין צדוקין מודין בו התם בהעראה שלא כדרכה:
edits.english: Atypical intercourse is also written, etc. - This implies that the Sadducees agree to it. But in the chapter 'One of the Laws of Monetary Matters,' regarding one who erred concerning an adulterer and adulteress, it implies that the Sadducees do not agree to it there, concerning ha'ara'ah in an atypical manner.

edits.hebrew: דאמרי כדרכה אסירא אפילו העראה - דהאי דכתיב את מקורה הערה בכדרכה:
edits.english: Where they said: In the typical manner, even ha'ara'ah is forbidden - For that which is written 'he has uncovered her fount' refers to the typical manner.

edits.hebrew: אי הכי - מאי איריא דקתני שהורו בשומרת יום כנגד יום? אפילו נדה נמי כי האי גוונא קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת הוא, והוי בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בו:
edits.english: If so - why specifically does it teach that they ruled concerning a woman who observes a day for a day? Even a niddah in such a case is a partial fulfillment and partial nullification, and it would be a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree.

And they answer: They say thus: In the typical manner - even ha'ara'ah is forbidden. In an atypical manner - it is the completion of intercourse that is forbidden, but ha'ara'ah is permitted. And they ask: If so, even a niddah herself during her menstrual period would also be permitted, and they would say that only the completion of intercourse is forbidden. So why does the mishna state that they erred concerning a woman who observes a day for a day!

edits.hebrew: אלא לעולם בכדרכה - דאמרי בשומרת יום העראה שריא אפילו בכדרכה, וגמר ביאה הוא דאסיר. ודקאמרת הא העראה כתיב, דאמרי העראה באשה נדה הוא דכתיב ולא בשומרת יום. הלכך לא מתוקמא בנדה אלא בשומרת יום, והוי בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין בה:
edits.english: Rather, actually, in the typical manner - For they say that regarding a woman who observes a day for a day, ha'ara'ah is permitted even in the typical manner, and only the completion of intercourse is forbidden. And what you said, 'Behold, ha'ara'ah is written,' they say that ha'ara'ah is written regarding an afflicted woman (niddah during her menstrual period) and not regarding a woman who observes a day for a day. Therefore, it is not established regarding a niddah, but rather regarding a woman who observes a day for a day, and it is a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree.

edits.hebrew: ואי בעית אימא - דקאמרת שומרת יום הא כתיבא, הא לא קשיא, דכי קתני כגון דאמרי זבה לא הויה אלא [היכא דחזיא] ביממא כדכתיב כל ימי זובה, אבל היכא דחזיא בליליא טהורה. והוא הדין לשומרת יום דאמרי דהוא היכא דקא חזיא ביממא דהיינו בימי זיבה. הלכך לא מתוקמא בנדה אלא בשומרת יום ובזבה, והויא הוראה בדבר שאין הצדוקין מודין:
edits.english: And if you wish, say - What you said, 'Behold, a woman who observes a day for a day is written,' this is not difficult. For when it teaches, it is for example when they say that a zava is only when she sees during the day, as it is written: 'all the days of her discharge,' but if she sees at night, she is pure. And the same applies to a woman who observes a day for a day, for they say that it is when she sees during the day, which is during the days of her discharge. Therefore, it is not established regarding a niddah, but rather regarding a woman who observes a day for a day and a zava, and it is a ruling concerning a matter with which the Sadducees do not agree.

Rather, actually, it is concerning ha'ara'ah in the typical manner, and they say: Ha'ara'ah with an afflicted woman (see there, 18), a niddah during her menstrual period, is what is written, and not concerning a woman who observes a day for a day. And if you wish, say instead that they say: A woman assumes the status of a zava (who discharges blood from her source, not during her menstrual period) is only during the day and not at night, as it is written: “All the days of her discharge” (Leviticus 15:26).
And if she saw blood at night, she is not impure (Rashi). Or, one who sees during the day has the status of a zava, and at night she is like a niddah (Rach).

edits.hebrew: הכתיב כל ימי זובה - הני מילי לאתויי קרא קמא דכתיב זוב דמה ימים רבים:
edits.english: It is written: “All the days of her discharge” - This refers to bringing the first verse, where it is written: 'the discharge of her blood for many days'.

And immediately they ask: We learned in the mishna: There is a prohibition against performing prohibited labor on Shabbat written in the Torah, but one who carries out objects from one domain to another is exempt. And they ask: According to Shmuel, and why are they liable? With regard to carrying out, isn’t it written: “Neither carry a burden out of your houses” (Jeremiah 17:22), and the Sadducees agree to it!
Passing or throwing - These are not explicitly written.

And they answer: They say: Carrying out is what is forbidden, but carrying in from the public domain to the private domain is permitted. And if you wish, say instead that they say: Carrying out is what is forbidden, but passing or throwing from one domain to another is permitted.

But if the court erred in a matter that is not explicitly stated in the Torah and is not the uprooting of the entire essence, then they bring an offering, and all those who performed the transgression are exempt from individual sin-offerings. For example, if they said that there is a prohibition against carrying out on Shabbat but not the law of passing, or if they permitted bowing to an idol when it does not involve extending hands and feet. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 14:2).

edits.hebrew: דאמרי הוצאה אסירא והכנסה שריא - ותנא הוצאה הכנסה קרי לה, כדאמרינן במסכת שבת (ב:) ובמסכת שבועות (ה.):
edits.english: Where they said: Carrying out is forbidden and carrying in is permitted - And the Tanna refers to carrying out as carrying in, as we say in Tractate Shabbat (2b) and in Tractate Shevuot (5a).

edits.hebrew: איכא דאמרי הוצאה והכנסה (שריא) [הוא דאסירא] אף על גב דהכנסה לא כתיבא, סברא היא: מה לי אפוקי מה לי עיולי (שבת צו.):
edits.english: Some say that carrying out and carrying in [are forbidden], even though carrying in is not written, it is a logical inference: what difference is there between taking out and bringing in (Shabbat 96b).

And furthermore, we learned in the mishna: There is a prohibition against engaging in idol worship written in the Torah, but one who bows to the idol is exempt. And why should they be liable? Is not one who bows explicitly written, as it is written: “You shall not bow to another god” (Exodus 34:14)!
Bowing in an atypical manner - For example, bowing to Pe'or or to Markulis.

edits.hebrew: השתחואה - בפשוט ידים ורגליים כדכתיב (בראשית י״ט:א׳) וישתחו אפים ארצה:
edits.english: Bowing - with the extension of hands and feet, as it is written (Genesis 19:1): 'and bowed down with their faces to the ground'.

And they answer: They say: When bowing is forbidden, it is in its typical manner, when this is the way of worship for this idol. But in an atypical manner, where one does not bow to it, it is permitted. And if you wish, say instead that they say: Bowing itself, it is in its typical manner that it is forbidden. And when is that? When it involves the extension of hands and feet, which is a complete bowing like in the Temple. But bowing that does not involve the extension of hands and feet is permitted.
